summary.headline: JTL Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47.5% YoY to INR693 crore on a record 1,23,262 MT quarterly volume; FY27 guided to about 30% volume growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR693 crore (up 47.5% YoY, 47.2% QoQ), with EBITDA of INR58 crore and PAT of INR38 crore, and the company reported record quarterly and annual volumes. Management attributed the volume jump mainly to higher utilisation at the Mangaon facility and DFT structural steel pipes, with no channel-inventory gain. FY26 totals were revenue INR2,136 crore, EBITDA INR166 crore, PAT INR103 crore and volume 3,95,900 MT. Management guided to about 30% FY27 volume growth, while the 2 million tonne capacity target by FY27 was reiterated but the Aryan Bhatia question flagged that the earlier 6 lakh tonne FY27 guidance has effectively been reduced after capex delays.

financial_highlights.change: Management says Q4 EBITDA/ton ~INR4,700 per analyst question; about INR150 higher QoQ

segments.name: Mangaon facility (Maharashtra)
segments.commentary: Utilisation at about 35-40% currently; Q4 volume uplift of about 20,000-25,000 MT came entirely from Mangaon, versus a usual run rate of about 1 lakh MT a quarter. Management targets 60-70% utilisation at Mangaon this year.

segments.name: DFT structural steel pipes
segments.commentary: Main growth driver in Q4 and exports; being empanelled with customers, and ACRS certification obtained for Australia, with US and Canada being explored.

segments.name: JTL Defence (formerly RCI Industries; copper, brass, phosphor bronze alloys)
segments.commentary: Taken over in December; Q4 revenue of about INR15 crore with a stated 20% EBITDA margin, which management called not a fair steady-state number due to inventory gains. Production about 100 MT in Q4, 150 MT/month run rate now, and 500 MT/month targeted by exit FY26; FY27 revenue target INR150-200 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume growth of about 30% YoY, described as achievable on current capacity; management said it may revise upward once new capacity comes on stream.
EBITDA per ton growth of 10-15% in FY27, taking it from INR3,900 to about INR4,500-4,800; longer-term aspiration of INR5,000/ton.
Capacity target of 2 million tonnes by FY27 reiterated (from 1 million tonnes today); cold rolling/color-coated complex at Mangaon with 7 lakh tonne outlay to be fully running by end of H1 FY27.
FY27 capex of about INR100-120 crore: INR60-70 crore in H1 for remaining expansion and INR30-40 crore maintenance in H2.
ROCE expected to recover to about 25-30% in coming years as CWIP assets are capitalised; operating cash flow expected positive by FY28 (next financial year).
JTL Defence: 10-15% EBITDA margin targeted in coming quarters; defence capacity of 700-800 MT/month by FY29.
capex_capacity: Mangaon cold rolling complex (color-coated pipes, GT pipes) with 7 lakh tonne outlay; nearing completion, full running by end of H1 FY27.
Company capacity to rise from 1 million tonnes to 2 million tonnes; majority capex done, remaining about INR60-70 crore in H1 FY27.
All further capacity addition is at Maharashtra; no other facility additions planned.
Utilisation guidance not given for FY27 because new products keep starting at different rates; to be updated next quarter.
Capacity delays attributed to rains and complexity of the color-coated capex; the outlook timeline has slipped as a result.
demand_pricing: Management says market is on a good track after the November duty introduction led to price corrections, then price rises and stocking; a slowdown in the first week of the quarter due to state elections, followed by a pick-up.
Seasonality: H1 typically slower due to monsoon and new project announcements; H2 typically stronger, though the pattern has weakened in recent years.
Revenue per ton is driven by HRC cost, which has risen; color-coated products will carry higher revenue per ton once volumes start.
DFT pipes were priced at discounts in some places to push the new product, which pressured margins.
Management said there is no import steel pressure in Q1 FY27, and no inventory gain in Q4 FY26.
Export margin is not superior to domestic; export premium is roughly INR6,000-8,000/ton at the general level, with the benefit being volume scale rather than margin.

qa_highlights.question: What was the value-added share in Q4 sales mix and what drove Mangaon volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added products were about 27% of Q4 sales; Mangaon accounted for the entire 20,000-25,000 MT uplift above the usual ~1 lakh MT/quarter run rate, with DFT pipes the driver.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 volume growth guidance reliable given the Q4 run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to about 30% YoY growth on current capacity, and said it would revise the target after the new capacity comes on line; a 1-2 month slip is possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the earlier 6 lakh tonne FY27 / 9 lakh tonne FY28 guidance implied to be lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed capex delays for the color-coated complex, including rains and other factors; the outlook has been pushed out and a clearer picture is expected by end of next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is JTL Defence's margin and revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 margin of 20% was called not fair due to inventory gains; 10-15% margin is targeted, with FY27 revenue of INR150-200 crore and a 500 MT/month exit run rate.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to the end of the heavy capex cycle and expects positive operating cash flow by next financial year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised EBITDA/ton and ROCE outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 EBITDA/ton expected at INR4,500-4,800 (10-15% growth); ROCE expected at 25-30% over the coming years as assets are capitalised.

risks_watch: Delays in the Mangaon color-coated/CRM capex: management has already slipped the timeline and the FY27 volume and capacity outlook depends on it.
Margin pressure from DFT discounting and steel price volatility (HRC cost rising); EBITDA/ton guidance is qualified as hard to pin down.
Mangaon utilisation at 35-40% now versus 60-70% target for FY26-end; DFT panel empanelment and export certifications need to keep converting.
Operating cash flow has been negative for 2-3 years and debt rose in FY26; positive OCF is only expected by FY28.
JTL Defence margin of 20% in Q4 was inventory-driven; the sustainable margin is still unproven, and the business is at an early stage after the NCLT-linked acquisition.
Q1 FY27 demand may be seasonally weak in the monsoon period; the second quarter is guided by monsoon conditions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, volume and the DFT and export story, but noticeably defensive on timelines: several answers conceded capex delays and declined to give utilisation or precise EBITDA/ton guidance. Management was most evasive on the revised capacity timeline and on the 6 lakh tonne FY27 figure from the prior quarter.
key_quotes: 30% is something that we'll definitely achieve.
So as the capex is delayed, the outlook is delayed as well.
There is no absolute inventory gain in this quarter.
We should be drifting close to 25% to 30% ROCE for the next years, given that a lot of our assets are not sweating and a lot of capex is happening.

adds.what: Mangaon cold rolling / color-coated complex (7 lakh tonne outlay), taking company capacity from 1 million to 2 million tonnes

growth.why: Management guides about 30% FY27 volume growth, said achievable on current capacity (Mangaon utilisation 35-40%, targeted 60-70%), with the 7 lakh tonne Mangaon cold-rolling complex to be fully running by end H1 FY27, but the capacity timeline has slipped due to capex delays.
